Jehudi
jeh-HOO-dye
proper noun
Hebrew Yehudi (H3065), a Jew or a man of Judah — the ordinary gentilic used as a personal name; his great-grandfather is called Cushi, an Ethiopian name.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

Jehudi the son of Nethaniah appears in one chapter and does one thing, and it is among the worst deeds recorded of a servant in Scripture. The princes first sent him to fetch Baruch and the roll so that they could hear it for themselves (Jer 36:14). Then the king sent him to fetch the roll from Elishama's chamber, and Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king (Jer 36:21). It was winter, and there was a fire on the hearth. And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed (Jer 36:23). The knife in the hand is Jehoiakim's by command, and the text keeps the responsibility at the throne; but the hand that read the word of God aloud and then cut it up was Jehudi's. His name means simply a Jew. The man named for the covenant people destroyed the covenant word, three or four leaves at a time, and neither the king nor his servants were afraid, nor rent their garments (Jer 36:24).

Origin & Era

The officer of Jehoiakim who read Jeremiah's roll before the king and cut it with a penknife into the fire; his name means a Jew.

JEHUDI, Hebrew Yehudi, a Jew, a man of Judah.

Son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi.

Sent by the princes to fetch Baruch and the roll of Jeremiah's words.

Sent by the king to fetch the roll out of Elishama the scribe's chamber, and he read it before the king.

When he had read three or four leaves he cut it with the penknife and cast it into the fire.

Key Scripture

Jer 36:14 — "Therefore all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, unto Baruch, saying, Take in thine hand the roll wherein thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch the son of Neriah took the roll in his hand, and came unto them."

Jer 36:21 — "So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll: and he took it out of Elishama the scribe's chamber. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king."

Jer 36:23 — "And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth."

Act 5:29 — "Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men."

Modern Corruption

Obeying orders is offered as a defence; Jehudi read the word of God aloud and then cut it up, and Scripture records his name.

expand to see more

Jeremiah 36 puts two kinds of servant in the same room. Three princes asked the king to stop and were refused. One officer took the penknife. The king is the one the chapter condemns most heavily — the sentence against Jehoiakim is that he should have none to sit upon the throne of David and his dead body cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night (Jer 36:30). But the text does not let the instrument disappear into the command. It names him, twice, and tells us exactly what he did with his hands.

Scripture nowhere accepts the plea that a man was only carrying out instructions. We ought to obey God rather than men (Act 5:29) is the rule where the two conflict; Saul's footmen refused to fall on the priests of the LORD at his order, and their refusal is recorded to their credit (1Sa 22:17); the midwives of Egypt disobeyed Pharaoh and God dealt well with them (Exo 1:17-20). The principle to recover is that lawful authority is real and is to be honoured, and that its writ stops precisely where it commands what God forbids. Every man answers for his own hands, and the fact that someone senior wanted it done has never once been a defence at the bar of God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yehudi (H3065), a Jew, a man of Judah; used here as a personal name.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yehudi (H3065) — the officer of Jehoiakim; Jeremiah 36:14, 36:21, 36:23.

Hebrew Yehudah (H3063) — Judah, praise; the tribe and kingdom from which the gentilic comes.

Hebrew taar (H8593) — a knife, a razor; he cut it with the penknife (Jer 36:23).

Hebrew ach (H254) — a fire-pot, a hearth; the brazier burning before the king in the winter house.

Hebrew qara (H7167) — to rend, to tear; yet they were not afraid, nor rent their garments (Jer 36:24).

Usage

"“All the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah… unto Baruch”."

"“And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king”."

"“He cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth”."
